claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain in fusion plasma-facing materials is predominantly governed by grain-boundary-mediated deformation.
High-temperature toughness in fusion plasma-facing materials is predominantly governed by grain-boundary-mediated deformation.
A fine-grained microstructure enhances grain-boundary sliding at high temperature relative to a coarse-grained microstructure.
Enhanced grain-boundary sliding improves plastic flow and toughness.
Thermomechanical processing can produce fine- and coarse-grained states of the same alloy while composition and overall phase distribution are held constant.
Temperatures at or above 1200°C are relevant high-temperature test conditions for fusion plasma-facing refractory materials.
Fine-grained material has a higher grain-boundary density than coarse-grained material.
Increased grain-boundary density facilitates grain-boundary sliding.
Grain-boundary mobility increases at elevated temperature.
Greater grain-boundary mobility allows boundaries in fine-grained materials to slide and accommodate deformation.
Grain-boundary sliding increases plastic strain before failure.
Grain-boundary activity dissipates energy more effectively than brittle crack propagation and therefore improves toughness.
Under identical high-temperature mechanical loading, fine-grained samples will exhibit significantly greater plastic strain than coarse-grained samples.
Under identical high-temperature mechanical loading, fine-grained samples will exhibit significantly greater toughness than coarse-grained samples.
Deformed fine-grained samples will show grain-shape changes and boundary offsets indicative of active grain-boundary sliding.
Coarse-grained material has lower plastic strain and toughness because grain-boundary sliding is less effective.
Coarse-grained material has a greater tendency toward brittle failure under the stated test conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies to tungsten-based or refractory alloys designed for plasma-facing applications under high-temperature conditions.
The mechanism may not apply to materials with fundamentally different compositions or phase distributions.
Nanostructured reinforcements may activate deformation mechanisms other than grain-boundary sliding.
